## The problem

UMatch explores matching ride requests to nearby drivers within a streaming
window. The engineering challenge begins before the matching step: historical
taxi-trip records describe completed trips, rather than continuously available
drivers and waiting riders.

The [repository's documented design](https://github.com/raxit65535/umatch)
constructs separate rider and driver-location streams, then joins plausible
candidates for matching. The existing project record uses Python, Kafka,
Spark Structured Streaming, and a presentation layer.

## Three design decisions

### 1. Construct the input streams

The project uses taxi-trip records and synthetic information to simulate two
unbounded streams. Timestamps provide a basis for processing windows, but they
do not provide a shared rider/driver identity key.

### 2. Narrow the candidate join

An unrestricted Cartesian join compares every rider with every driver in a
window. The documented approach instead introduces location-based keys through
geohashes, grouping geographically nearby candidates before matching.

### 3. Apply greedy distance matching

Within those groups, the project applies a greedy assignment using a
Haversine-distance condition. This is an engineering trade-off rather than a
claim of globally optimal matching. Group boundaries, windowing, unmatched
requests, and local density are relevant to interpreting the approach.

The architecture illustration connects stored data, Kafka, stream processing,
and the presentation components. The source repository, slides, and recorded
demo provide the supporting implementation material.

## What a fuller evaluation should document

A reproducible evaluation would identify data selection and simulation rules,
window sizes, grouping parameters, workload density, baselines, hardware, and
matching quality as well as latency. The repository includes historical project
material, but this page does not turn it into a newly reproduced benchmark.
